```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(psych)
library(paran)
library(lavaan)
library(mice)
```

Now that our data are useable, we need to look at the factor structure of the Autism Quotient (AQ) and to select the autism items to be retained for the remaining analyses. 

```{r}
survey_original_FU2 = read.csv("survey content FU2.csv")

AQ_FU2 = survey_original_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(contains("AQ"))

AQ_imputed_results_FU2 = mice(AQ_FU2, seed = 1234)
AQ_imputed_FU2 = complete(AQ_imputed_results_FU2,2)
AQ_imputed_FU2 = data.frame(ID = survey_original_FU2$ID, AQ_imputed_FU2)
write.csv(AQ_imputed_FU2, "AQ imputed FU2.csv")
```

```{r}
survey_FU2 = read.csv("AQ imputed FU2.csv") %>% dplyr::select(-X, -ID)
```

The first step is to look at the internal consistency and performance of the AQ factors. Note that I am not entirely confident as to why certain items were excluded when examining these factors beyond replication from Zhu et al., (2022). 

Social Discourse Convention Items, to look at internal consistency of 1) the original Social Discourse convention items from Zhu et al. (2022); 2) all Social Discourse Convention items, including items from BAAP

```{r}
##Zhu (2022) Social Discourse Convention Items 
survey_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._1:AQ._3) %>% corr.test()
survey_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._1:AQ._3) %>% performance::item_intercor()
survey_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._1:AQ._3) %>% psych::alpha()

##all Social Discourse Convention items, including items from BAAP
survey_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._1:AQ._7) %>% performance::item_intercor()
survey_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._1:AQ._7) %>% psych::alpha()


```

Interest in Details/Pattern Items, to look at internal consistency of 1) the original Interest in Details/Pattern items from Zhu et al., (2022); and 2) all Interest in Details/Pattern items, including item from IASQ

```{r}
##Zhu (2022) Interest in Details/Pattern Items 
survey_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._8:AQ._12) %>% corr.test()
survey_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._8:AQ._12) %>% psych::alpha()

##all Interest in Details/Pattern Items, including item from IASQ
survey_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._8:AQ._13) %>% psych::alpha()

```

Imagination Ability Items, to look at internal consistency of 1) the original Imagination Ability items from Zhu et al., (2022); 2) all Imagination Ability items

```{r}
##Zhu (2022) Imagination Ability Items 
survey_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._14:AQ._18) %>% corr.test()
survey_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._14:AQ._18) %>% psych::alpha()

##all Imagination Ability Items
survey_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._14:AQ._20) %>% psych::alpha()


```

Social Cognition Items, to look at internal consistency of 1) the original Social Cognition items from Zhu et al., (2022); 2) all Social Cognition items

```{r}

##Zhu (2022) Social Cognition Items 
survey_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._21:AQ._25) %>% corr.test()
survey_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._21:AQ._25) %>% psych::alpha()

## all Social Cognition Items
survey_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._21:AQ._28) %>% corr.test()
survey_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._21:AQ._28) %>% psych::alpha()

```

Social Anhedonia Items; note that all items were retained in the present study. 

```{r}
##Zhu (2022) Social Anhedonia Items; all items retained for the present study too
survey_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._29:AQ._34) %>% psych::alpha()
```


Original AQ measures

Original AQ measures are referring to the items from Zhu et al., (2022) (excluding AQ items loading onto desire for predictability/routine, which were not included in the present study). 

```{r}

##Again, AQ original include items that were from Zhu et al., (2022)
AQ_original_FU2 = survey_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._1:AQ._3, AQ._8:AQ._12, AQ._14:AQ._18, AQ._21:AQ._25, AQ._29:AQ._34)
#AQ_original = survey %>% dplyr::select(AQ._1:AQ._3, AQ._9:AQ._14, AQ._18:AQ._22, AQ._27:AQ._30, AQ._36:AQ._41) %>% dplyr::select(-AQ._20, -AQ._21, -AQ._29) ## not sure why this version of AQ_original excludes items 20, 21 and 29? They were retained in Zhu et al (2022) and in FU2

```

Determine number of factors using Parallel Analysis 

```{r}
paran(AQ_original_FU2, cfa=FALSE, graph=TRUE,
      color=TRUE, col=c("black", "red", "blue"))
```

Results suggest that five factors emerge from the Original AQ (from Zhu et al).

Now we run Principal Axis Factoring using five factors and extract the factor loadings and communalities. We can also look at the p-value, degrees of freedom, Chi-square, TLI, CFI, and RMSEA to examine fit. 

```{r}
mod_original_PAF_FU2 = fa(AQ_original_FU2, nfactors = 5, fm = "pa") ##Principal Axis Factoring
?fa()
write.csv(mod_original_PAF_FU2$loadings, "original PAC loading FU2.csv")
write.csv(mod_original_PAF_FU2$communality, "original PAC commu FU2.csv")

mod_original_PAF_FU2$PVAL
mod_original_PAF_FU2$dof
mod_original_PAF_FU2$chi

mod_original_PAF_FU2$TLI
1 - (1 - mod_original_PAF_FU2$TLI)* mod_original_PAF_FU2$dof / mod_original_PAF_FU2$null.dof
mod_original_PAF_FU2$RMSEA
```


Original AQ Exploratory Factor Analysis with five factors and maximum likelihood factor analysis.

```{r}
AQ_EFA_mod_original_FU2 = fa(AQ_original_FU2, nfactors = 5, fm = "ml")
write.csv(AQ_EFA_mod_original_FU2$loadings, "original EFA loadings FU2.csv")
write.csv(AQ_EFA_mod_original_FU2$communalities, "original EFA comm FU2.csv")

AQ_EFA_mod_original_FU2$PVAL
AQ_EFA_mod_original_FU2$dof
AQ_EFA_mod_original_FU2$chi
AQ_EFA_mod_original_FU2$RMSEA


AQ_EFA_mod_original_FU2$TLI
1 - (1 - AQ_EFA_mod_original_FU2$TLI)* AQ_EFA_mod_original_FU2$dof / AQ_EFA_mod_original_FU2$null.dof

```

Confirmatory factor analysis with with Original AQ items only. 

```{r}

##CFA using only items from Zhu et al., (2022)
CFA_AQ_original_spec_FU2 = "
social_anhedonia =~ AQ._29+AQ._30+AQ._31+AQ._32+AQ._33+AQ._34 
detail_pattern =~ AQ._8+AQ._9+AQ._10+AQ._11+AQ._12
social_cog =~ AQ._21+AQ._22+AQ._23+AQ._25
discourse_convention =~ AQ._1 +AQ._2+AQ._3
imagination =~ AQ._14+AQ._15+AQ._16+AQ._17+AQ._18

social_anhedonia~~detail_pattern
social_anhedonia~~social_cog
social_anhedonia~~discourse_convention
social_anhedonia~~imagination
detail_pattern~~social_cog
detail_pattern~~discourse_convention
detail_pattern~~imagination
social_cog~~discourse_convention
social_cog~~imagination
discourse_convention~~imagination
"

cfa_mod_original_FU2 = cfa(CFA_AQ_original_spec_FU2, AQ_original_FU2)
summary(cfa_mod_original_FU2, standardized=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)
write.csv(round(inspect(cfa_mod_original_FU2,what="std")$lambda,2), "aq original cfa FU2.csv")
```


New AQ Measures 

These analyses include all 33 AQ items that were administered in FU2

```{r}
#AQ_imputed = survey %>%  dplyr::select(-AQ._20, -AQ._21, -AQ._29, -X, -AQ._9, -AQ._12, -AQ._15, -AQ._19, -AQ._23, -AQ._24, -AQ._35, -AQ._7, -AQ._16)

```

```{r}
paran(survey_FU2, cfa=FALSE, graph=TRUE,
      color=TRUE, col=c("black", "red", "blue"))
```

Above results also indicate that there are 5 AQ factors 

Now we run Principal Axis Factoring using five factors and extract the factor loadings and communalities, which are saved as csv files. We can also look at the p-value, degrees of freedom, Chi-square, TLI, CFI, and RMSEA to examine fit.

```{r}
mod_new_PCF_FU2 = fa(survey_FU2, nfactors = 5, fm = "pa")

#write.csv(mod_new_PCF_FU2$loadings, "new PAF loadings FU2.csv")
#write.csv(mod_new_PCF_FU2$communality, "new PAF comm FU2.csv")

mod_new_PCF_FU2$TLI
1 - (1 - mod_new_PCF_FU2$TLI)* mod_new_PCF_FU2$dof / mod_new_PCF_FU2$null.dof
mod_new_PCF_FU2$RMSEA

mod_new_PCF_FU2
```



New AQ Exploratory Factor Analysis with five factors and maximum likelihood factor analysis. 

```{r}
AQ_EFA_mod_new_FU2 = fa(survey_FU2, nfactors = 5, fm = "ml")


#write.csv(AQ_EFA_mod_new_FU2$loadings, "new EFA loadings FU2.csv")
#write.csv(AQ_EFA_mod_new_FU2$communality, "new EFA comm FU2.csv")

AQ_EFA_mod_new_FU2$PVAL
AQ_EFA_mod_new_FU2$dof
AQ_EFA_mod_new_FU2$RMSEA

AQ_EFA_mod_new_FU2$chi

AQ_EFA_mod_new_FU2$TLI
1 - (1 - AQ_EFA_mod_new_FU2$TLI)* AQ_EFA_mod_new_FU2$dof / AQ_EFA_mod_new_FU2$null.dof

AQ_EFA_mod_new_FU2$loadings
summary(AQ_EFA_mod_new_FU2)

```

Now rather than having individual AQ items, we compute the means of each subscale.  

```{r}

social_discourse_convention_FU2 = AQ_imputed_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._1, AQ._2, AQ._3, AQ._4, AQ._5, AQ._6, AQ._7) %>% rowMeans()
pattern_FU2 = AQ_imputed_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._8, AQ._9, AQ._10, AQ._11, AQ._12, AQ._13) %>% rowMeans()
imagination_FU2 = AQ_imputed_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._14, AQ._15, AQ._16, AQ._17, AQ._18, AQ._19, AQ._20) %>% rowMeans()
social_cognition_FU2 = AQ_imputed_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._21, AQ._22, AQ._23, AQ._25, AQ._26, AQ._27, AQ._28) %>% rowMeans()
social_anhedonia_FU2 = AQ_imputed_FU2 %>% dplyr::select(AQ._29, AQ._30, AQ._31, AQ._32, AQ._33, AQ._34) %>% rowMeans()

AQ_scores_FU2 = data.frame(ID = survey_original_FU2$ID, social_discourse_convention_FU2, pattern_FU2, imagination_FU2, social_cognition_FU2, social_anhedonia_FU2)

write.csv(AQ_scores_FU2, "AQ scores FU2.csv")
```


Finally, the CFA for the new AQ, which includes all 33 AQ items administered in FU2. 

```{r}
CFA_AQ_new_spec_FU2 = "
social_anhedonia =~ AQ._29+AQ._30+AQ._31+AQ._32+AQ._33+AQ._34 
detail_pattern =~ AQ._8+AQ._9+AQ._10+AQ._11+AQ._12+AQ._13
social_cog =~ AQ._21+AQ._22+AQ._23+AQ._25+AQ._26+AQ._27+AQ._28
discourse_convention =~ AQ._1 +AQ._2+AQ._3+AQ._4+AQ._5+AQ._6+AQ._7
imagination =~ AQ._14+AQ._15+AQ._16+AQ._17+AQ._18+AQ._19+AQ._20

social_anhedonia~~detail_pattern
social_anhedonia~~social_cog
social_anhedonia~~discourse_convention
social_anhedonia~~imagination
detail_pattern~~social_cog
detail_pattern~~discourse_convention
detail_pattern~~imagination
social_cog~~discourse_convention
social_cog~~imagination
discourse_convention~~imagination
"

cfa_mod_new_FU2 = cfa(CFA_AQ_new_spec_FU2, AQ_imputed_FU2)
summary(cfa_mod_new_FU2, standardized=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)
write.csv(round(inspect(cfa_mod_new_FU2,what="std")$lambda,2), "aq new cfa FU2.csv")
```
